questions.3.question.back: What can a close view show about the past, but a wide view might hide?

questions.5.question.back: A young person learns a skill from an older person. They make it better. Then they teach it to their friends. What is this called?
questions.5.question.source: A young person learns a skill from an older person. She makes it better. Then she teaches it to her friends. What is this called?

questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Right. In collective learning, people share what they know, make it better, then pass it on. This is how knowledge grows.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. In collective learning, people share what they know, make it better and pass it on. This is how knowledge grows.

questions.6.question.back: Archaeologists found these clues at a site of ancient humans. Which clue could show what people cooked?
questions.6.question.source: Archaeologists found these clues at early human sites. Which clue could show what people cooked?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: The handprints on a rock wall

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. These tools may show that people shared ideas. They do not show what people cooked. Look back at Lesson 5.

questions.7.question.back: After a good harvest, a farming village might have a surplus. What is a surplus?
questions.7.question.source: After a good harvest, a farming village may have a surplus. What is a surplus?

questions.7.options.0.text.back: More food than is needed right now

questions.7.options.0.text.source: More food than people need right now

questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Right. A surplus is extra food. People can store it, so not everyone has to farm.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A surplus is extra food. People can store it, so not everyone has to farm.
